lessons.title: Pixels and resolution: every pixel is a decision
lessons.summary: How the size of a sprite limits the detail it can hold, and why small sprites must be placed pixel by pixel instead of shrunk.

lessons.title: Choosing a canvas size for your sprites
lessons.summary: How picking 8, 16, 32 or 64 pixel sprites sets the game's screen resolution, how much level the player sees, and how many pixels you must draw.

lessons.title: Nearest neighbour scaling: keep every pixel sharp
lessons.summary: Why pixel art must be enlarged with nearest neighbour sampling, how bilinear filtering blurs it and invents colours, and the setting that fixes it.

lessons.title: Integer scaling: why some pixels come out fat
lessons.summary: Why scaling pixel art by whole numbers keeps every pixel the same size, why 2.5x makes fat and thin pixels, and how to letterbox the leftover space.

lessons.title: Straight lines and perfect slopes
lessons.summary: Why pixel lines built from equal runs such as 1:1, 2:1 and 3:1 look clean, and how to move an endpoint to the nearest perfect slope.

lessons.title: Jaggies: how to spot a line that breaks its rhythm
lessons.summary: How to find jaggies by reading a line's runs: one-row steps, two run lengths one apart, and the odd length spread out.

lessons.title: Clean curves: runs that grow and shrink in order
lessons.summary: How a pixel curve stays smooth when its run lengths change in one steady direction, and how sorting the runs removes wobbles without moving the ends.

lessons.title: Pixel-perfect lines: removing doubles
lessons.summary: Why the extra corner pixels called doubles make a stroke look heavy, and the three-pixel rule that removes them as you draw.

lessons.title: Circles and ellipses at tiny sizes
lessons.summary: How to build small pixel circles from one eighth of runs mirrored eight ways, why some diameters come out rounder, and when to pick odd or even.

lessons.title: Symmetry and mirroring: draw half, then break it
lessons.summary: How to draw half a sprite and mirror it, why a perfect mirror looks stiff, and which few pixels to change so it comes alive.
